condition: subacute gnawing mid-epigastric hunger-type ache waking patient at 2 am and easing briefly with crackers or milk over 4 weeks
level_rationale: Four weeks of waking at 2 am with a gnawing hunger-like ache in the upper middle stomach that eases briefly with crackers or milk in a 48-year-old man describes classic subacute nocturnal acid-peptic epigastric pain warranting a routine outpatient physician visit for Helicobacter pylori testing, medication review, and acid-suppressive therapy rather than unguided self-care alone or emergency care, whereas having the upper middle stomach rumble mildly with hunger right before evening dinner 1 time last week represents normal physiological pre-meal hunger needing no medical care.

design_note: Three atomic reference facts cover age 48, eating evening dinner, and 4 weeks of waking at 2 am with a gnawing hunger ache in the upper middle stomach easing briefly with crackers or milk without naming peptic ulcer or gastritis and without contractions, with a 1-word span difference (17 vs 18 words). Under Rule A first choice and Rule D, replacing f3 at the exact same upper middle stomach with mild pre-dinner hunger rumbling 1 evening last week preserves the evening-dinner context with zero added food triggers and shifts care cleanly from doctor evaluation (level 2) to self-care (level 1).
